title: Vibration Trend Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Vibration Trend Record within the Maintenance Prognostics Database. Analyzes equipment condition and estimates maintenance needs with uncertainty bounds. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record reads condition signals over time, fits a trend, and projects when that trend reaches a maintenance threshold. Every projection carries uncertainty bounds, because a point estimate without bounds overstates what is known. A prognosis triggers inspection or maintenance planning; it never replaces inspection.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: readings: [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A maintainer uses these records to schedule work before a failure instead of after it, and to explain, with bounds shown, why a given maintenance window was chosen. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Vibration Trend Record: project a condition trend to its maintenance threshold.
readings = [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]
threshold = 45.0
slope = (readings[-1] - readings[0]) / (len(readings) - 1)
remaining = (threshold - readings[-1]) / slope if slope > 0 else float("inf")
print("readings:", readings)
print("trend per step:", round(slope, 2))
print("latest reading:", readings[-1], "threshold:", threshold)
print("estimated steps to threshold:", round(remaining, 1))
print("uncertainty bounds steps:", round(remaining * 0.8, 1), "to", round(remaining * 1.25, 1))
demo_output:
readings: [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]
trend per step: 1.5
latest reading: 30.6 threshold: 45.0
estimated steps to threshold: 9.6
uncertainty bounds steps: 7.7 to 12.0

fields.bound_method: uncertainty bounds shown with the projection

This record documents Fleet Comparison Record within the Maintenance Prognostics Database. Analyzes equipment condition and estimates maintenance needs with uncertainty bounds. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record reads condition signals over time, fits a trend, and projects when that trend reaches a maintenance threshold. Every projection carries uncertainty bounds, because a point estimate without bounds overstates what is known. A prognosis triggers inspection or maintenance planning; it never replaces inspection.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: readings: [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A maintainer uses these records to schedule work before a failure instead of after it, and to explain, with bounds shown, why a given maintenance window was chosen. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked compounded. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: buildable-now. Implementation status: buildable-now. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Fleet Comparison Record: project a condition trend to its maintenance threshold.
readings = [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]
threshold = 45.0
slope = (readings[-1] - readings[0]) / (len(readings) - 1)
remaining = (threshold - readings[-1]) / slope if slope > 0 else float("inf")
print("readings:", readings)
print("trend per step:", round(slope, 2))
print("latest reading:", readings[-1], "threshold:", threshold)
print("estimated steps to threshold:", round(remaining, 1))
print("uncertainty bounds steps:", round(remaining * 0.8, 1), "to", round(remaining * 1.25, 1))
demo_output:
readings: [20.1, 21.6, 23.1, 24.6, 26.1, 27.6, 29.1, 30.6]
trend per step: 1.5
latest reading: 30.6 threshold: 45.0
estimated steps to threshold: 9.6
uncertainty bounds steps: 7.7 to 12.0

fields.bound_method: uncertainty bounds shown with the projection
